name: Hyoscine butylbromide
executiveSummary: Hyoscine N-butylbromide (Buscopan). Adult spasm/antisecretory: **20 mg IV/IM/SC** up to **3–4 times/day** (max ~**100 mg/day**); PO **10–20 mg**. Pediatrics by age/weight. Anticholinergic.
indications:
## Indications

- GI spasm / colic.
- Secretion reduction (palliative / perioperative) as adjunct.

## Precautions

- Contraindicated in angle-closure glaucoma, myasthenia gravis, megacolon/mechanical obstruction.
- Potentiates anticholinergics; antagonizes metoclopramide on the GI tract.
- Distinguish from **scopolamine (hyoscine hydrobromide)** — different doses.

> Local ampoules often **20 mg/mL**.

adulto.dose: Spasm / antisecretory: **20 mg IV, IM or SC** up to every 6–8 h (usual max **100 mg/day**). PO: **10–20 mg every 6–8 h**.
adulto.administration: Slow IV (~5 min) diluted or per card; IM/SC; PO. Ampoule may be given PO in some protocols.
adulto.notes: Watch tachycardia, urinary retention, blurred vision.

pediatrico.dose: IV/IM/SC antisecretory: infants/<6 years **0.3–0.6 mg/kg/dose** (orient. max **1.5 mg/kg/day**); 6–12 years **5–10 mg** up to 3/day; >12 years **20 mg** up to 4/day. PO: 6–12 years **10 mg every 8 h**; >12 years **20 mg every 6 h**.
pediatrico.notes: Follow institutional ceilings; avoid in glaucoma/myasthenia.

adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Dry mouth, tachycardia, blurred vision, constipation, urinary retention, allergic reactions.
